findings.title: Final HTTP status and bodyless-response semantics
findings.resolution: The public final-response path accepts only status 200–599. HEAD, 204, 205 and 304 each have explicit producer suppression, direct-write, Content-Length and trailer rules; status-specific restrictions still apply to HEAD. Native framing owns the resulting response.
findings.verification_boundary: Specification/declaration recheck; actual wire framing remains B15/B17/B22 product work.

findings.title: HTTP wire metadata and decoded binary gRPC metadata are distinct
findings.resolution: HTTP metadata retains its wire values. A separately owned gRPC projection performs bounded Rust Adapter comma splitting, SP/HTAB edge trimming, empty-segment preservation, per-name order preservation, entry/byte/scratch preflight and atomic rollback before per-segment public Tonic from_headers/get_bin/to_bytes decoding. No managed base64 decoder or nonexistent Tonic splitting behavior is assumed.
findings.verification_boundary: Pinned public Tonic source seams independently inspected; private util configuration read only to establish padding behavior. No new gRPC runtime test.

findings.title: Trusted forwarding requires one coherent bounded proxy chain
findings.resolution: Only explicitly trusted direct peers enable the three X-Forwarded fields. Field counts and aligned bounded lists are validated together; right-to-left trusted-hop processing is bounded and publication is atomic. Original wire Host/Origin and peer identity remain available and MCP authorization is not bypassed by forwarded values.
findings.verification_boundary: Design/security-boundary review; no claim of product penetration or network conformance execution.

findings.title: Every successful ordinary HTTP path finishes before cleanup
findings.resolution: MapRaw, generated void/Task, custom ServerResult and middleware short-circuit success join the one idempotent CompleteAsync/response_finish before OnCompleted, registered disposal, scope disposal and dispatch completion. Untouched status is 200; explicitly selected status is preserved. Failures do not send a second final response. Cleanup remains LIFO, failure-isolated and independent of cancellation. Protocol-owned paths use typed protocol terminals; denied MCP retains its documented HTTP exception.
findings.verification_boundary: Complete semantic path recheck and consumer compilation evidence; automatic native completion is a future B15/B16/B22 witness.

findings.title: Streaming result ownership transfers at successful execution admission
findings.resolution: The caller retains the source until a single-use execution claim succeeds. The cleanup finally is installed before later fallible work; an admitted suppressed HEAD result still disposes its transferred source. An unexecuted or replaced result retains caller ownership, and the producer example opens its source only during execution.
findings.verification_boundary: Static ownership/consumer review; no product streaming execution claimed.

findings.title: Protocol contexts cannot bypass typed framing or MCP pre-parse authentication
findings.resolution: gRPC exposes only safe request metadata/services/identity/items/time/cancellation/abort plus completion/disposal lifecycle. Raw body/JSON/trailers and all raw HTTP response access including HasStarted and OnStarting are rejected; local or inherited ServerFilter is rejected at freeze. Auth denial uses gRPC16/7 without DTO/business admission. MCP dispatch kind2 applies the managed pre-parse gate to every method; kind3 uses the same ticket and reserved continuation without a second take, scope, auth chain or final dispatch completion. Pending HTTP denial cannot become Allow; post-Allow protocol output belongs to rmcp. Nested managed-work leases and native retirement prevent early cleanup under cancellation.
findings.verification_boundary: Independent state-machine and cross-layer mapping review. The cross-language gate, framing restrictions and retirement races remain explicit B18/B19/B22 product obligations.

findings.title: Metadata ownership transfer is distinct from borrowed views
findings.resolution: bound_addresses transfers one metadata owner. metadata_headers and metadata_grpc_headers borrow only while an owner lease remains live. Wrappers copy decoded metadata before releasing that lease, and binary public values are owned arrays rather than escaped native views. Wrong-owner-kind operations return empty outputs and a deterministic error.
findings.verification_boundary: ABI/declaration ownership review, including current 48-export prototype/layout evidence; no product interop execution.

findings.title: MCP schemas preserve non-null object roots and nested nullability
findings.resolution: Tool roots must have static finite object metadata; Nullable<T>, scalar/array/dictionary/open/polymorphic roots are rejected. A root-only exporter transform narrows reference DTO object|null to object without changing nested nullability. Registration has finite metadata/schema/scratch bounds; successful null results are rejected. The finite BCL witness preserves its initial failing nullable-value-root attempt and final seven positive/five negative-root checks.
findings.verification_boundary: Witness tests BCL static metadata only, not NativeWeave registration, network MCP or AOT execution.

findings.title: Retained inbound owners cannot create an awaited payload-credit cycle
findings.resolution: Both read and write payload admission use complete request/global backing-capacity grants without waiting or retrying. Partial credit, queue reservations and managed/native copy overlap roll back on failure. Queue/network waits hold only their documented bounded state and remain separate. Taken chunks retain actual backing-capacity charges after dispatch until last release. The 128x32KiB/4MiB and cross-request global exhaustion cases require immediate resource_limit rather than deadline-based progress. D18, D20, the current body-retirement design and both visible and unrendered B16 fields now agree; the historical awaited-permit experiment remains preserved and explicitly superseded as product policy.
findings.verification_boundary: Reasoned liveness counterexample and independent exact-policy recheck. No product quota coordinator was executed; B16/B17/B22 own the implementation witnesses.

findings.title: Timeout and body-limit precedence must resolve identically in both ABI records
findings.resolution: New section2.1 defines endpoint-over-default generic timeout selection, gRPC minimum with method timeout and admission-time client deadline, and one monotonic whole-call budget. TimeSpan ticks convert to checked uint64 nanoseconds with a positive 24-hour maximum. gRPC/MCP reject explicit generic body/JSON modifiers and use protocol-specific limits; per-direction cumulative payload units exclude framing but not its separate budget. route and protocol descriptor values must agree; protocol max_json_bytes=0 means unavailable HTTP JSON binding, not unlimited JSON. Server XML descriptions now agree.
findings.verification_boundary: New finding discovered and independently rechecked by this reviewer; compilation/export regenerated after the XML change. Runtime option-freeze validation remains future implementation.
